extracted.intended_audience: students of rhetoric and literature; writers and critics seeking to produce or evaluate 'the Sublime' in prose and poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating sublime literary/rhetorical writing: how to choose material, deploy passion and metaphor, preserve unity, and aim at lasting greatness rather than transient applause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and moral integrity of the critic
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics must be 'liberal and impartial' and not biassed by avarice or bribery when judging great works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the critic's life is 'controlled by bribery' or 'measured by his own interests', his verdict cannot be trusted. Literary evaluation presumes a moral freedom from personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent: strive for solid advantage, not mere applause
rubrics_metrics.description: One should apply oneself to work not 'with a view to pleasure or applause, but for that solid advantage which is worthy to be striven for and held in honour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with aims beyond immediate popularity—seek lasting value and honour rather than temporary applause or pleasurable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passions as central to literature and the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: The passions play an important part in literature generally and especially in relation to the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ and portray passions deliberately: pathos and emotional force are key contributors to sublime effect (the treatise promises a separate work on the passions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of art; some effects require natural genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parts of literature 'are in the power of natural genius alone' and 'must be learnt from no other source than from art' (i.e., some effects cannot be manufactured purely by technique).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that technique can train and refine, but some sublime qualities depend on native genius and cannot be fully taught as formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pretentious straining after grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: Extravagance that is mere 'straining after grandeur' (ludicrous pretension) must be distinguished from genuine strength of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute bombast or artificial magnification for authentic force; excess that reads as pretension undermines sublimity (example: Cleitarchus’s extravagance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select borrowings discriminately; avoid indiscriminate plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarists 'show no discrimination in their pilferings, seizing what comes first to hand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If borrowing, do so with judgment and purpose; indiscriminate patching-in of material damages coherence and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the most striking circumstances and remove superfluity
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer should 'choose the most striking circumstances par excellence, and having relieved them of all superfluity' concentrate on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select striking details and strip away extraneous matter so that the elevated parts stand out; economy enhances sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain unity; avoid interpolations/patches that mar the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpolations or 'patches or rents' in a work 'mar altogether the effect'—sublimity arises from details 'built up in an uninterrupted series'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure continuity and organic development; avoid grafting unrelated passages or stylistic patches that break the flow and diminish overall power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for posterity; be in advance of your times
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer 'should always work with an eye to posterity'—a book 'in advance of its own times' will endure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim beyond contemporary fashions and transient tastes; lasting works anticipate or transcend current judgments and so survive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rise to the dignity of your subject and cover cardinal points
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of Caecilius: he 'fails to rise to the dignity of his subject' and 'misses the cardinal points'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat great subjects with appropriate scale and seriousness; address the central issues rather than getting lost in trivialities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical utility—tell how to achieve effects, not only definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Caecilius is blamed for 'wasting energy in tedious attempts to define the Sublime, but [not] tell[ing] us how it is to be attained.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorizing should be accompanied by concrete, practical guidance for attaining the effect (technique, examples), not merely abstract definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the Pathetic (pathos) when treating the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure 'to deal with the Pathetic' is a serious omission in a work on the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing pathos—how to move and affect the reader emotionally—is essential to a full account of sublimity; do not neglect it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metaphors judiciously—be flexible, avoid arbitrary numeric limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement in source: 'He allows only two metaphors to be employed together in the same passage (XXXII. ii.)' (criticized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rigid, arbitrary rules (e.g., 'no more than two metaphors'); instead let rhetorical devices serve the effect—use as many metaphors as clarity, force, and taste require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid frigid conceits and hollow pedantry
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorical conceits and 'hollow pedants' produce frigid, unnatural expressions (examples: talking of 'vultures as “living tombs”').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of cold, artificial conceits and technical ostentation that call attention to themselves rather than to the subject; favor natural, convincing imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer vivid illumination over sweeping, dull generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: To 'illumine a large subject' vividly (like a landscape lighted by lightning) is preferable to 'sweep[ing] away' a subject in dull breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, illuminating images and moments of clarity to make large subjects intelligible and striking rather than relying on broad, lifeless generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid harsh, broken, or discordant style and gratuitous conceits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors like Hegesias are criticized for a 'harsh and broken' style and for indulging in conceits that parody finer models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for stylistic harmony and coherence; avoid mannerisms that produce a fractured or jarring reader experience.
